messages:
emily: Quick update — I addressed the requested changes on the canary rollout config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/832. Reduced initial canary weight, added a rollback timeout, and included unit tests. Squashed commits. Please take a quick look when you have a few minutes.

raj: Thanks — will eyeball in ~30. main question: does the canary cooldown interact with autoscale cooldowns?

emily: Good call. I added a note in the PR: the cluster autoscale cooldown remains the default (10m) but the canary controller uses an independent 5m cooldown window so they don't block each other. See the diff for the new field: `canary.cooldown_minutes: 5`.

jessica: Saw the tests — one flaky on windows runner, pushed a tiny fix in a follow-up commit to normalize time zones.

andre: LGTM aside from the autoscale clarification. Also can you add a single line to the release notes about the canary timeout? keeps the SREs informed.

emily: Added release-note blurb and updated the squash commit message to include the ticket and revert instructions. Squashed now. I can hold the merge if you want one more SME check @raj.

raj: I'll run a quick smoke against staging and kick off the canary-bot check.

canary-bot: Canary health check initiated for PR #832 — baseline comparisons in progress. Expected latency variance <2%.

raj: Smoke passed locally and basic traces look clean. canary-bot shows no regressions so far. Approving now. :shipit:

emily: Awesome — planning to merge at the next low-traffic window (00:00 UTC) to minimize impact, will tag oncall.

oncall: Noted — I'll watch the rollout. Ping me if error rate goes >0.5% or latency +10% for >5m.

emily: Thanks everyone — merging on schedule unless anyone objects within the hour.
